summary: jenscolt's base as one parametric bowl: skin, wall, rim and the front leg windows; his inside is left out (N2 puts our mechanism there).

parts.name: base
parts.role: the bowl the body and mechanism sit in, ground part
parts.why_separate: the only part of this design
parts.print_orient: bowl up, foot on the bed

assembly.check: stands on its foot, open side up

options: outer and inner skins sewn with a top ring
alternatives.choice: outer and inner skins sewn with a top ring
alternatives.why: the cut of two near-parallel lofts took 40 s and came out invalid; the sewn shell builds in 6 s

acceptance.text: the bowl is within the default fidelity limits of the reference both ways
every sweep variant (S 0.65, wall and section 0.8x / 1.2x) is one valid closed solid
the bowl, its rim and the front windows look like jenscolt's base
bowl skin and wall thickness separate parameters
the rim notches (leg windows) as named features, one parameter set mirrored left/right
not: build.py reads a mesh: the reference meshes are read only by the gates and the designer's probes
the default fidelity gate passes, the sweep's variants are valid solids, and the judge scores ≥ 0.70 against the mesh
